reply_text:
I found five candidates from 2020. Four come from transcripts I opened and read. The fifth, the New York Times "five years" claim, I could only read in a news report.

- **1 December 2020, Axel Springer Award.** Musk said he was "extremely confident" Tesla would reach full autonomy and release it to customers in 2021, and confirmed he meant Level 5. In the same talk he said almost all new cars would have full autonomy within about ten years. Asked about Ray Kurzweil's date for the singularity, he answered, "I think you're saying he is predicting 2025. I think that is reasonably accurate." Two things to check there. The 2025 date is Musk's own; it isn't in the question as transcribed. Kurzweil's published date for the singularity is 2045, not 2025. This transcript was made by a fan site from the event video, so it isn't official.
- **21 October 2020, Tesla third-quarter earnings call.** Musk said Tesla hoped for a "wide release" of the Full Self-Driving beta by the end of 2020. The Motley Fool transcript doesn't name the speaker at each line; these lines are in the remarks it credits to Musk.
- **25 July 2020, New York Times interview with Maureen Dowd.** The Times page wouldn't open for me. I read the claim only in an AI News article, which reports him saying AI "could overtake humans by 2025" and quotes him with a "five years" line. The fuller quote ("less than five years from now") appeared only in a search snippet, so I haven't used it.

Nothing I read matches the claim you already have on file (9 July 2020, Level 5 basic functionality this year), so none are marked as already recorded. One lead I didn't open: search snippets show that on the 22 July 2020 earnings call Musk was "very confident" Full Self-Driving would be functionally complete by the end of 2020. That looks close to your recorded claim.

I left out two Neuralink forecasts from his May 2020 Joe Rogan podcast. They're about a brain implant, not AI. I used 9 of the 12 searches and all 6 page openings. The New York Times page was blocked, and the rev.com Rogan transcript cut off after the opening lines.
